**Source: same external audit @ `2ec47d8`. Independently re-verified, measured.** `season?: ActiveSeasonGoalInfo` (`StudentDialog.tsx:414`) defaults to `DEFAULT_SEASON_INFO` (`:424`); `StudentsTab.tsx:317-324` documents omitting it *specifically* to avoid "a false ordering dependency" with T091, which is **Passed** (ledger `:171`). The blocker cleared; the follow-through was never filed — the deferral lived only in a module comment, which is exactly the failure constitution item 20 exists to prevent, recorded here as a fifth instance of it. **Fifth instance of the defect family** behind three of the owner's four production bugs: optional prop + plausible fixture default + call site passing nothing (after `OutreachEventDialog.teams`, `ScheduleMeetingsDialog.teams`, `CoachHome.seasonId`, `Leaderboard.seasonId`). **Why it is latent rather than visible, which is also why nothing caught it:** `DEFAULT_SEASON_INFO` is `{ defaultGoalHours: 100 }` and the real column default is `not null default 100`, so the fixture is indistinguishable from correct until a season is created with a different goal — at which point the student dialog silently uses 100. **Sequencing with T151:** `StudentDialog` carries a *fourth* optional-prop-with-fixture-default that T151's premise did not account for. **CORRECTION 2026-08-04.** This row comes from the **same external audit (`2ec47d8`) that was measured wrong on T161, T162, T163 and T321** — it counted **files named `<module>.test.ts`** rather than tests *of* a module. **Measured today, at least two of its ten named loaders already have dedicated test files:** `attendance.ts` (**12** tests) and `students.ts` (**23** tests, re-measured at `6c8b2dd` after T198 reworked that loader). The remaining eight (`teams`, `kiosk`, `seasons`, `invites`, `parents`, `accept`, `selfCheckoff`, `leaderboard_privacy`) have no dedicated file, but that is **not** the same as untested — T163 showed a loader can be covered entirely by its importers. **Do not treat this as ten untested loaders. Measure invocation, not filenames, and split the row by what is actually uncovered.** **Original row text follows.** **Source: external audit @ `2ec47d8`, "explicitly out of scope for this pass".** `teams.ts`, `kiosk.ts`, `attendance.ts`, `seasons.ts`, `students.ts`, `invites.ts`, `parents.ts`, `accept.ts`, `selfCheckoff.ts`, `leaderboard_privacy.ts`. Recorded as one row rather than ten, to be split when picked up. Context from T146's measurement: **81** `as …DbRow` casts across the loader directory, each able to hide an omitted column exactly as the `teams.color` bug did, against **zero** tests in the directory before T146. Roughly ten real sites use `.select('*')`, where a cast cannot hide an omission. The structural remedy — generated Supabase `Database` types, which would let the compiler catch omitted columns and make the casts unnecessary — remains unavailable (no generated types in repo; `client.ts`'s single `createClient` passes no `Database` generic) and is a separate, larger decision than any of T161–T167.

name: T168 — the placeholder-default sweep covered 7 sites; src/pages/ and src/components/ are unswept
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T168`

**Type / provenance:** Audit (continuation) — **discovery only**

**Title:** the placeholder-default sweep covered 7 sites; `src/pages/**` and `src/components/**` are unswept

**Status at migration:** Filed

---

**BOUNDARY, added 2026-07-30 after the owner caught the orchestrator conflating the two halves.** T168 is **discovery only: it finds instances and produces findings. It fixes nothing.** Every instance found becomes its own work task through the normal worker→checker pipeline — as the five already found demonstrate: T151 (three dialogs' `teams`), T155 (`CoachHome.seasonId`), T158 (`Leaderboard.seasonId`), T159 (`StudentDialog.season`), T170 (`OutreachList.viewerStudentId`). So "finish T168" is a misleading phrase: completing the sweep leaves the whole remediation outstanding. **Consequence for delegation:** a plan-only session can perform T168's discovery and hand back drafts, but it cannot complete this row's remediation successors, and it must not be told it owns T168 — the orchestrator owns the row, the numbering, and every fix. Findings arrive as `docs/swarm/inbox/<branch>.md` and are folded in here. **Remediating the *mechanism* rather than the instances is separate work and is filed as T172.** **SWEEP RESULT, 2026-07-30 — `src/pages/**`/`src/components/**` is now covered** by external audit `claude/audit-batch-2` @ `c962b7f`, folded in and re-verified. It found **two** new confirmed instances (`StudentHome`'s three props → T176; `SubscribePopover.functionsBaseUrl` → T177), swept ~40 components clean with the per-component reasoning recorded in `docs/swarm/inbox/claude-audit-batch-2-t168-sweep.md`, and correctly declined to double-count `CoachHome.teamId` (already deferred by T155) and two props on unreachable components. **T168 is discovery-complete for the identity-placeholder shape. It is NOT complete for the class**, because verifying it surfaced a second shape the discriminator cannot see: a **function-typed default pointing at a fixture loader** (`ParentHome`, filed T181 — swept clean by the audit, yet its dashboard is entirely fabricated). Both shapes are the same defect; the second is harder to spot because `loadX` matches the codebase's legitimate DI convention. **A second discovery pass is needed for the fixture-loader shape before T168 can close**, and T172's mechanism must catch both or it will certify files like `ParentHome.tsx` as clean.

name: T171 — T154's no-stale-frame property is true in the code and pinned by nothing
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T171`

**Type / provenance:** Debt / test integrity

**Title:** T154's no-stale-frame property is true in the code and pinned by nothing

**Status at migration:** Filed (item 20, from T154's PASS)

---

**MINOR carried from T154's PASS, measured by the checker and worth more than its grade suggests.** Moving the re-seed out of the render body into a `useEffect` keyed on `[user, lastSeededUserId]` — a change that demonstrably reintroduces a stale frame — leaves **all 36 tests passing**. The property IS true in the shipped code (measured: commits are `["none:dark","user-bob:light"]` shipped vs `["none:dark","user-bob:dark","user-bob:light"]` under the mutation, the middle entry being Bob signed in with Alice's theme still on screen), but nothing would notice if it broke. **Two independent causes, both instructive.** (1) `RecordingProbe` consumes only `useThemeMode()`, and the provider's `useMemo(() => ({mode, refresh}), [mode, refresh])` memoizes the consumer away when `user` changes but `mode` does not — so a stale commit is structurally invisible to it. Only a **dual-context** recorder (`useThemeMode()` **and** `useAuth()`) can see it. (2) The test literally named `the stale theme never reaches the DOM even for one frame during the switch` does `renders.slice(beforeSwitch).filter((m) => m !== 'dark')` and asserts on the survivors — **it filters out the very value it should assert absent**, so `['dark','light']` passes. **This is the round-1 failure shape recurring inside the one test written to prevent it**, which is why it is filed rather than logged. Fix: dual-context recorder asserting `not.toContain('user-bob:dark')` on commits after the switch, and drop the `.filter`. Acceptance: moving the re-seed into a `useEffect` must fail the suite; it currently does not. The checker also corrected itself here — its own first strict `not.toContain('dark')` probe reported no stale frame under the mutation and was worthless for the same structural reason.

name: T172 — make the placeholder-default class structurally hard to reintroduce, instead of sweeping for it forever
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T172`

**Type / provenance:** **Debt (mechanism)** — actual work, not an audit

**Title:** make the placeholder-default class structurally hard to reintroduce, instead of sweeping for it forever

**Status at migration:** Filed

---

**Filed 2026-07-30 because the owner caught the orchestrator treating "audit the class" and "fix the class" as one thing.** T168 finds instances; T151/T155/T158/T159/T170 fix individual instances; **nothing yet stops the sixth pattern becoming a seventh.** Every instance has the identical shape — an optional prop, a plausible fixture default, and a call site that passes nothing — and it has produced **three of the owner's four production bugs**, plus two more found only by audit. The instance-by-instance approach cannot converge: `src/pages/**` and `src/components/**` are still unswept, and a new component added tomorrow can reintroduce it with a green suite. **Candidate mechanisms, to be chosen in the packet, not here.** (a) A lint rule or `tsc`-level check flagging an optional prop whose default is a module-level fixture constant — cheap, mechanical, runs on every commit, and directly encodes the discriminator. (b) Generalise T151: make these props **required** wherever a fixture default exists, which the T151 probe measured as far cheaper than feared (34 TS2741 errors, **zero in production source**, all in two test files) — the compiler then enforces it permanently. (c) Naming convention plus a grep gate, weakest of the three. **Prefer (b) then (a):** (b) is enforcement by the type system rather than by a convention someone must remember, and today's measurement shows the cost is a test-file change, not a refactor. **A fourth shape, found during T176:** the same *metric* coalesce is duplicated in TypeScript in **four** places (`StudentHome.tsx:815`, `HoursTab.tsx:449`, `csvExport.test.ts:372`, `CoachHome.tsx:979 sumGoalHours`) against **one** SQL definition in `v_student_goal_projection`. T176's MAJOR was one instance of exactly this, and consolidating the four is the general form of that fix. **Sequenced after T151** so the pattern is proven on three real dialogs before being generalised, and after T168 so the true instance count is known rather than estimated. Relates to `architecture-review-parallelism.md` §3.2, which argues the same case for turning a judgement into a computed property.

name: T188 — two different "confirmed hours" numbers exist in the app and can legitimately disagree
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T188`

**Type / provenance:** Data consistency (product question) — **DIAGNOSED 2026-08-05; VALID, and the row understates it: FOUR divergences, not one**

**Title:** two different "confirmed hours" numbers exist in the app and can legitimately disagree

**Status at migration:** Filed

---

**Found while verifying T170's constitution-item-3 question; not a T170 defect and not blocking it.** `v_student_hours` (`metric_views.sql:3-19`) computes confirmed hours from **`attendance`** — real check-in/check-out timestamps, `status in ('present','late')`, joined to completed sessions on events that count volunteer hours. `computeStudentHours` (`OutreachList.tsx:1184-1203`) computes them from **RSVP status `going`** on a session whose status is `completed`, and never touches `attendance` at all. **These answer different questions** — "did they show up and check in" versus "did they say they were going and did the session happen" — so item 3 is not violated and T170 is unblocked. **But a student who RSVPs `going` and does not attend accrues hours on `/outreach` and none in `v_student_hours`**, so the same student can see two different hour totals on two screens. `computeStudentHours`'s heuristic is disclosed (BEH-02), so this is a deliberate design that has drifted rather than a bug — but nothing reconciles the two, and the owner is the one who would field the question. Cheap to resolve: either name them differently on screen, or make the outreach page read the attendance-backed number. **DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-05 — validity confirmed, scope is WIDER than filed. No code changed.** **A hypothesis worth killing first:** T201 (merged same day) fixed a two-numbers-disagree bug in the same family, so it might have dissolved this. **It did not** — T201 was roster filtering (`is_active`); T188 is RSVP-vs-attendance. Different mechanism entirely; checked before any work. **The row's own finding still holds, verified against current code:** `computeStudentHours` (`OutreachList.tsx`) still computes confirmed hours from RSVP `status = 'going'` + session `status = 'completed'`, and still never touches `attendance`. **But THREE more divergences exist that the row does not name, and two hit NORMAL usage:** **(2) `hours_override` is invisible to it.** `v_student_hours` honours it first in its coalesce; `computeStudentHours` uses raw session length, so any coach adjustment diverges. **(3) check-in/check-out clamping is invisible to it.** A student who arrives late or leaves early gets the clamped span in `v_student_hours` and the FULL session length on `/outreach`. Neither number is wrong; nothing on screen says they answer different questions. **(4) it counts NON-OUTREACH events — MEASURED, not inferred.** A probe called `computeStudentHours` with a completed MEETING session and a `going` RSVP: it returned **2.0 confirmed hours**. The function takes only `(studentId, sessions, rsvps)` — it has no access to event `type` or `countsVolunteerHours`, so it CANNOT filter — and `loaders/outreach.ts:739` queries `events` for the season with **no type filter**, with no JS filter between. **This directly contradicts T322's ruling** (*"volunteer hours = `type = 'outreach'` ONLY"*), which landed AFTER T188 was filed, so the row could not have known. **Honest limit of the measurement:** the probe proves the FUNCTION counts a meeting and the loader applies no type filter. It does not render the live page, so "a meeting's hours appear on screen for a real user" is inferred from those two facts, not observed. **Owner ruling needed — the row's two suggested fixes point opposite ways:** (a) **name them differently on screen** (cheap, honest, keeps both numbers, but the `/outreach` figure keeps contradicting T322); (b) **make `/outreach` read the attendance-backed number** (one number everywhere, but that page's whole purpose is planned-vs-confirmed from RSVPs, which attendance cannot express). **Divergence (4) may be separable from the product question** — making `computeStudentHours` respect `type = 'outreach'` is arguably just conforming to an existing owner ruling rather than a new decision, and could ship without settling (a)/(b).

**The data half is DONE and this row overstated the problem until now.** The owner repointed the rows directly in SQL after the import; confirmed 2026-08-05 from the live app rather than from the record — the KPI strip shows **337.8 volunteer hours** and **Vine Street Market** under the active **2026-27 FIRST CANOPY** season, which is the imported data rendering. (341.75 → 337.8 is T322 excluding non-outreach types, not loss.) **The orchestrator had called this "the highest-value untouched row" on 2026-08-05 reading `Filed` from this ledger; that was wrong and is retracted — the record was stale, the world had moved.** **WHAT REMAINS, and it is much smaller:** `scripts/migrate/transform.ts:70-84`'s `buildSeasonUpsert` still hardcodes `is_active: false` and `MIGRATION_SEASON_NAME = '2025–2026'`, and the ETL still takes **no `--season-id`/`--season-name` argument and prints no post-run notice** (verified by grep across `scripts/migrate/`). So a future import repeats the same silent surprise and needs the same manual SQL repair. **Priority: low** — it only bites on the next import, and the caution itself is defensible (`seasons_single_active_idx` permits one active season; a migration should not hijack it). **The fix is to make it loud, not to change the default:** either accept a target season argument, or print a named warning identifying the inactive season it created and the `update` needed to repoint.

name: T600 — aggregateParticipationRows and aggregateParticipationForStudent are the same MET-01 arithmetic maintained in t
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T600`

**Type / provenance:** Debt (duplicated metric formula, two TypeScript copies of one SQL view) — **found by T162's premise gate round 1**

**Title:** `aggregateParticipationRows` and `aggregateParticipationForStudent` are the same MET-01 arithmetic maintained in two files

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-03 by the W3-A orchestrator in auto-mode (item 20); see `auto-mode-decisions.md`, "W3-A auto-mode window"**

---

**Measured, not inferred.** `meetings.ts:465-489` and `checkin.ts:340-373` both re-implement `v_student_participation`'s expression in TypeScript: same summing, same `Math.max(expectedCt - excusedCt, 1)` denominator floor, same `Math.round(x*10)/10` rounding. They differ only in that `checkin.ts`'s variant applies a season filter. The live view is `20260722000000_membership_views.sql:72-76` (W4's; `20260717000003_metric_views.sql:33-34` was superseded by a later `create or replace`). **Why this matters:** MET-01 is a number shown to a student about their own participation, and it is now maintained in three places — the view plus two TS copies — with no shared helper and no test asserting the copies agree. A change to the view (W4's file) silently desynchronises both. **Not a bug today** — the gate verified all three agree at `d5d420a`. **Do not fix inside T162**; that packet forbids editing `meetings.ts` and the consolidation touches W1's `checkin.ts` too, so it needs its own row and an ownership call. Cheapest credible scope: one shared exported helper the two callers wrap, plus a test asserting it against the view's own documented expression.

name: T507 — The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T507`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (responsive) — **found by the `layout-measurement` skill on its first run**

**Title:** The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-05 — MEASURED in real Chromium, not read from source**

---

`LoginPage.tsx:275` renders `<Card width={400} maxWidth="100%" padding={6}>`. **The author wrote the defensive `maxWidth` and it does nothing** — measured overflow by viewport: **320px → 40px · 360px → 20px · 375px → 13px · 390px → 5px · 414px and wider → 0**. So it affects most phones and worsens as the screen narrows; an iPhone SE is the worst case. **Presence-checked in the same run** (3 buttons, 2 inputs still rendered), so this is a real overflow and not the deleted-content artifact T325 caught. **Mechanism proven by walking the ancestor chain, not inferred:** the card is `rect=400 css-width=400px max-width=100%`, and its parent `.astryx-stack vertical` is **itself 400px with `max-width: none`** — so `100%` resolves against a box the card already sized, making the constraint a no-op. The first genuinely constrained ancestor is `.astryx-center` at 390px. **This is T325's exact mechanism on a second surface** (`maxWidth="100%"` resolving against an unconstrained parent, measured there as *no change*) — see T325's verification-log entry before packeting. **Candidate direction, not a prescription:** `maxWidth={400}` + `width="100%"` so the card fills the available width up to 400 rather than demanding 400 — but **measure it, do not assume it**; T325's obvious fix measured as a no-op. **No regression test is possible in jsdom** (no layout), so evidence is a before/after measurement, per the `layout-measurement` skill. **Not W2's surface** — `src/pages/login/**` belongs to no active workflow; needs an owner assignment before it is packeted.

---

The existing-tests rule lives as a **Non-Negotiables** bullet, while the numbered **Project-Specific Standards** list's actual item 10 is the **additive-migrations** rule. A 2026-08-06 decisions entry titles itself *"Boss ruling (constitution item 10)"* while ruling on a **test** amendment. Both readings are in active use. **Why this is more than tidiness:** "item 10 authorizes this" is the exact phrase that grants a worker permission to change a passed test, and this project has already had false authorizations (T148/T149) serious enough that a foreman refused to self-authorize on T510. A rule number that resolves to two different rules is a live hazard in the one place where being wrong is most expensive. The foreman correctly quoted the Non-Negotiables text verbatim rather than resolving the ambiguity itself, and forbade its worker from resolving it either. **Fix:** disambiguate in `constitution.md` — either number the Non-Negotiables separately or stop referring to tests as "item 10". name: T612 — mutation-replay's replay.py reports a genuine red replay as UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T612`

**Type / provenance:** Defect (shared tooling — **the anti-vacuity check itself is unreliable**) — found by T609's checker

**Title:** `mutation-replay`'s `replay.py` reports a genuine red replay as `UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests`

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-06**

---

**Measured.** `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py` printed `UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests` for a run whose **own captured output** showed `Failed Tests 1` with a real assertion failure (`expected [Function] to throw an error`, `ScheduleMeetingsDialog.test.tsx:1156`). Its summary parser read `failed=0 passed=0 skipped=56` off a vitest output shape it mishandles — a focused `-t` run, where the counter line reports skips separately. **Why this matters more than a parser bug:** mutation replay is this project's primary defence against a test that cannot fail, and the constitution leans on it (*"A gate that only reads is worth much less than one that runs"*). A false `UNTRUSTWORTHY` teaches agents to distrust and re-do valid replays — or worse, to accept the verdict and discard the evidence. T609's checker caught it only because it refused the tool's verdict and re-ran the mutation strictly by hand. **Shape:** fix the parser for the focused-run output shape, and make it fail loudly on an output it cannot parse rather than emitting a confident wrong verdict — the same rule T512 carries for ledger counts. **Cross-cutting; `.claude/skills/**` is W10's or the boss's surface, not W3's.**

name: T512 — WORKFLOWS.md's open-row counts are hand-recounted from the document itself; derive them from the ledger with a

**Filed because hand-recounting produced two wrong numbers in one PR.** `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`'s assignment table carries an open-row count per workflow. (2) The helper split the file into sections on `^## (W\d+) — `; W10 is the **last** workflow section, so its section ran to EOF and swallowed the Coordination-rules block-allocation table that follows, counting `T333`, `T600-699` and `T700-799` as W10 rows — W10 went 8 → 9 when the true figure was **6** (8 listed, T157 and T301 merged). Both defects are the same class: a count derived from prose, where a parsing miss produces a plausible number instead of an error. **The owner's framing, which is the fix:** *"the ledger is the only place a row's status actually lives, so counts belong derived from it — even a scripted count would beat hand-recounting a doc that four machines are appending to."* **Shape of the work:** a script reading `docs/swarm/task-ledger.md`'s pipe table (ID in column 1, Status in column 8), mapping each row ID to a workflow via the block allocation, and emitting open counts per workflow. Suggested Allowed Files: `scripts/**`, `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`. **MEASURED 2026-08-05, and it raises the bar for this row: the table is NOT column-consistent, so "Status is column 8" is not a safe parse.** Splitting all 278 `

description_md:

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-06, restated the same day. Source-verified. NOT blocked.**

---

**Scope, all verified in source on `main` and independent of any database:** (1) `student_teams` is written by **nothing** in the repo except the one-time backfill at `20260721000000_student_teams.sql:37` — verified across `src/`, `supabase/functions`, `scripts/` and every migration; no trigger, no edge function. Its sole application access is a `.select('team_id')` at `loaders/students.ts:482`. (2) `makeCreateStudent` (`:279`) and `makeUpdateStudent` (`:307`) write `students.team_id` only, so changing a student's team updates the badge and never the membership. (3) `StudentDialog.tsx` is single-select (one `teamId: string`), while `student_teams` is `primary key (student_id, team_id)` + `left_on` and the views are built for dual membership. (4) **Three roster filters do FUNCTIONAL single-team scoping** — `endMeeting.ts:340` (omits a dual-team student from the End Meeting roster entirely), `kiosk.ts:324`, `kiosk.ts:458` — the T187 defect class, live in three places. Note `kiosk.ts`'s `loadActiveStudentTeams` is misleadingly named: `queryActiveStudentTeams` (`:238-240`) selects from **`students`**. (5) Astryx ships `MultiSelector`, so the UI half is unblocked. ⚠️ **PRODUCTION DATA IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW AND WAS REMOVED FROM IT.** Three data-derived causes were filed and each was disproved by measurement: *students missing membership rows* (owner's query: **0** uncovered), *memberships pointing at archived teams* (**all 23 live**), and *most students inactive* (`kpi_views.sql:207` defines the strip's count as `count(*) from students where is_active`, which reads 22). A fourth — the observed Hours-by-team anomaly being season-scoping — was **not** pursued. **The owner then noted the database predates recent updates and has been through resets and manual edits, so it cannot testify about current code at all.** The dual membership found on George-Student (`test` + `Polytechnic Puzzle Pieces`, explaining 23 rows across 22 students) is therefore treated as development debris, not as a defect. **The earlier "students see an empty portal" severity claim is WITHDRAWN** — that student's `teamIds` scope to two teams with no matching upcoming events, so an empty Next up may simply be correct. **No user-facing defect is claimed by this row.** It is debt: the D018 work, scoped.

name: T806 — events/event_sessions RLS scopes by the legacy students.team_id, so a dual-team student never receives their s
description_md:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T806`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (RLS scoping divergence) — **filed 2026-08-07 while closing T199**

**Title:** `events`/`event_sessions` RLS scopes by the legacy `students.team_id`, so a dual-team student never receives their second team's events

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-07 (item 20). Needs a migration → OWNER APPLIES (item 16). Zero impact today.**

---

**Found while building T199's real `events` read, and T199 is what makes it observable** — before it the page had no rows at all, so nothing could be missing from them. `20260717000002_rls.sql:153-161`, verbatim: ```create policy own_or_linked_read on events for select to authenticated using (exists (select 1 from students s where s.id in (select my_student_ids()) and (events.team_ids is null or s.team_id = any(events.team_ids))));``` — and `event_sessions` (`:180-188`) inherits the identical test through `event_id`. **Both read the LEGACY single `students.team_id` column.** T187 (landed) moved `StudentHome` onto ACTIVE `student_teams` memberships (`StudentScope.teamIds`), so the page and the policy now scope by different sources. **They disagree for exactly one shape of user:** a dual-team student. An event scoped to `team_ids = {their SECOND team}` satisfies the page's `isEventInTeamScope` but is filtered out by RLS before it ever reaches the client — that student silently misses their second team's meetings, live check-in and sign-up opportunities. This is the SAME defect T187 fixed on the page side, still live one layer down. **Not the same as the withdrawn T804** — that row wrongly claimed `v_student_participation` scoped off `students.team_id` (it had already been migrated onto `student_teams` by `20260722000000_membership_views.sql`). These are RLS POLICIES, not views, and the grep is unambiguous: no later migration drops or replaces either policy. **Read from the policy text, NOT measured against a live database** — the text is unambiguous on this point, but the measurement was not run and this row should not be closed claiming it was. **Zero impact today:** every student in the system is single-team, and for them the two sources name the same team. **Scope, not yet designed:** a new additive migration replacing both policies' `s.team_id = any(...)` test with an ACTIVE `student_teams` membership test (`left_on is null`), matching what `membership_views.sql` already did for the views. Constitution item 10 forbids editing the applied `20260717000002_rls.sql`, so this is a NEW file using `drop policy if exists` + `create policy`, the route `20260720000001_avatar_storage.sql` already establishes for policy replacement. Needs an RLS assertion suite (the `sql` CI job now runs 12 steps) proving a dual-team fixture student sees BOTH teams' events. **Owner applies the migration (item 16).** Also check `attendance`/`rsvps` policies for the same pattern before designing — this row only verified `events` and `event_sessions`.

**Confirmed live, two surfaces disagreeing in the same session:** the left nav shows **Outreach 0**, while `/outreach` shows **"74 awaiting your RSVP"** and the student home banner reads **"You have 74 events to answer"**. **Cause:** `src/components/nav/SideNav.tsx:117` — `const PLACEHOLDER_OUTREACH_BADGE_COUNT = 0`, whose own comment says *"the real count is wired by T038"*. **T038 has PASSED and did not do it** — that row's checker note records it *"independently confirmed `SideNav.tsx` byte-unchanged"*, so the forward reference has been dangling ever since. This is the same dangling-forward-reference shape that left T199 unfixed for weeks, and the same placeholder-default family as T155 (`CoachHome`), T176 (`StudentHome`) and T181 (`ParentHome`); **T168 is the sweep that should have caught it and did not — worth a line in T168 rather than a separate finding.** **The computation already exists and must not be re-derived** (constitution item 3): `getUnansweredRsvpCount` (`OutreachList.tsx:1459`), signature `(sessions, rsvps, studentIds) => number`, already counts a `scheduled` session with no matching `rsvps` row per student. **Do NOT scope this as a one-line swap.** That signature is the whole difficulty: `SideNav` currently takes no data at all, so wiring it means giving the app-shell nav a real loader plus the viewer's resolved student ids — a new data dependency in the chrome, which is why T038 correctly declined to do it inline. Expect **STANDARD**, and expect the seam design (does the badge load its own data, or does `AppShell` thread it down?) to be the actual decision. **OWNERSHIP IS OPEN — the owner must assign it.** `src/components/nav/**` belongs to no workflow; the data is outreach (**W2**, CLOSED, 0 open rows) and the mount point is the shell (**W5**/W10 territory).
